questions.prompt: What is the primary responsibility of a **Database Administrator (DBA)**?

options.text: Ensuring database reliability, data integrity, performance, security, and recoverability
Replacing all SQL queries with text files
Disabling backups to save disk space

questions.prompt: Match each SQL statement family to its primary purpose.

columns.label: Define or alter tables, indexes, and constraints (`CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`)
Insert, update, or delete table rows (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`)

questions.prompt: Which relational constraint guarantees that every value in a child column matches an existing primary or unique key in a parent table?
Which properties make up the **ACID** guarantee in relational transactions? (Select all that apply.)
In database normalization, what does **Third Normal Form (3NF)** eliminate?

options.text: Transitive dependencies where a non-key column depends on another non-key column

questions.prompt: What does the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` clause enforce on a foreign key?

options.text: Sets the child foreign key to `NULL`
Prevents deleting a parent row while referencing child rows still exist

questions.prompt: Which SQL clause filters **grouped** rows after `GROUP BY` aggregation?
What is the main difference between `INNER JOIN` and `LEFT JOIN`?

options.text: `LEFT JOIN` keeps all rows from the left table even when no match exists on the right (`NULL`s for right columns)
`INNER JOIN` keeps unmatched rows from both tables
`LEFT JOIN` deletes unmatched rows from the left table

questions.prompt: Which clauses are valid in a standard SQL `SELECT` query? (Select all that apply.)
Why is a **B-tree index** the default index type in PostgreSQL and most relational databases?

options.text: It supports equality, range queries (`<`, `BETWEEN`), sorting (`ORDER BY`), and prefix `LIKE 'abc%'` efficiently
It stores the entire table in JSON

questions.prompt: What does `SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders;` return?
Which SQL statement adds a new column to an existing table without recreating the table?
Match each database engine category to its primary workload.

columns.label: High-concurrency, short read/write transactions with strict integrity
Large-scale scans, aggregations, and reporting over historical data
Sub-millisecond lookups for sessions, caches, and counters

questions.prompt: What does `COALESCE(discount, 0)` return when `discount` is `NULL`?
In SQL, what is the result of `NULL = NULL` in a `WHERE` predicate?

options.text: `UNKNOWN` (treated as falsey in `WHERE`; use `IS NULL` instead)

questions.prompt: Which practices help prevent accidental mass data loss during manual `UPDATE` or `DELETE` operations? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Wrap the change in `BEGIN` and verify affected rows before `COMMIT`
Run a `SELECT` with the same `WHERE` clause first
Omit the `WHERE` clause to make the query shorter
Take or verify a recent backup before risky migrations

questions.prompt: What does `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email);` enforce?

options.text: Emails must be shorter than 10 characters
No two rows can have the same non-`NULL` `email` value

code.source: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email);

questions.prompt: Which PostgreSQL command displays the estimated or actual execution plan of a query?
What is a **surrogate primary key**?

options.text: A system-generated identifier (such as an auto-increment integer or UUID) with no business meaning
A composite key made of 5 text columns

questions.prompt: Why should application services avoid connecting to the database as a `superuser`?

options.text: A SQL injection or bug could drop tables, read any schema, or bypass Row-Level Security

questions.prompt: Which items are essential parts of a reliable **backup and recovery** strategy? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Regularly testing restores on an isolated environment
Storing backups off-host / in separate failure domains
Defining RPO (Recovery Point Objective) and RTO (Recovery Time Objective)
Never verifying backups until an outage occurs

questions.prompt: What does **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)** measure?

options.text: Maximum time allowed to restore service
Number of CPU cores on the primary
Maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time (e.g., 5 minutes of transactions)

questions.prompt: What does **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)** measure?

options.text: Maximum acceptable data loss in gigabytes
Maximum acceptable downtime to restore the database to service

questions.prompt: In PostgreSQL replication, what is the role of the **Write-Ahead Log (WAL)**?

options.text: Recording every data page change sequentially before data files are updated, enabling crash recovery and replication

questions.prompt: Match each PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN` scan node to what it does.

columns.label: Reads every page of the table sequentially
Uses an index to locate matching TIDs and fetches rows from the heap
Satisfies the query directly from the index using the visibility map without heap fetches

questions.prompt: Which SQL query counts how many orders each customer placed?

options.text: `SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;`
`SELECT customer_id FROM orders ORDER BY COUNT(*);`

questions.prompt: What does `TRUNCATE TABLE logs;` do compared to `DELETE FROM logs;`?

options.text: Rebuilds every index one row at a time
Quickly deallocates all table data pages without scanning rows individually

questions.prompt: Which isolation anomaly occurs when Transaction A reads a row modified by Transaction B that later **rolls back**?
What is a **deadlock** between two database transactions?

options.text: Two transactions each hold a lock the other needs, so neither can proceed until the engine aborts one
A table with no primary key

questions.prompt: Which practices improve database **security** in production? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Using parameterized queries / prepared statements instead of string concatenation
Granting `PUBLIC` write access to all tables
Rotating credentials and storing them in a secret manager

questions.prompt: Why should queries avoid `SELECT *` in application code?

options.text: It transfers unnecessary columns, breaks Index Only Scans, and couples code to schema column order

code.source: SELECT order_id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid';

questions.prompt: What is a **Common Table Expression (CTE)** introduced by `WITH`?

options.text: A permanent physical table stored on disk
A named temporary result set scoped to a single SQL statement

questions.prompt: Which command checks active queries and wait states in PostgreSQL?
In `CREATE TABLE items (price NUMERIC(10, 2) CHECK (price >= 0))`, what does the `CHECK` constraint enforce?

options.text: No row can be inserted or updated with a negative `price`
`price` is automatically rounded to an integer
`price` is indexed with a hash index

questions.prompt: Why do **many-to-many** relationships require a junction (bridge) table in relational schemas?

options.text: A single column in one table cannot atomically store multiple foreign keys to the other table

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `ANALYZE` (updating table statistics) in PostgreSQL?

options.text: It collects row count and value distribution histograms so the query planner estimates costs accurately

questions.prompt: Which signals are key **database observability** metrics to alert on? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Connection pool saturation / active waiting sessions
Disk space exhaustion on data or WAL volumes
Font size in the DBA's terminal

questions.prompt: What does **logical** backup (`pg_dump`) produce compared to **physical** backup (`pg_basebackup`)?

options.text: SQL statements or archive dumps of schema and data that are portable across minor/major versions

questions.prompt: In a **primary-standby** replication setup, what is a **read replica** typically used for?

options.text: Offloading read-only analytical or reporting queries from the primary

questions.prompt: What happens when a `NOT NULL` column is added to an existing table without a `DEFAULT` when rows already exist?

options.text: The `ALTER TABLE` fails because existing rows would violate `NOT NULL`

questions.prompt: Why should **connection pooling** (e.g., PgBouncer) sit in front of PostgreSQL under high concurrency?

options.text: Each PostgreSQL backend is an OS process; hundreds of idle connections waste RAM and cause context-switch contention
Pools eliminate the need for indexes

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of **Idempotent** database migration scripts?

options.text: Re-running them safely converges to the same schema state without failing or duplicating changes
